chunks: Muḥammad ibn al-Fuḍayl narrated from Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام, who said:

The divorce of a slave, when he marries a free woman or marries a bondwoman belonging to other people, belongs to the slave himself. But if he marries the bondwoman of his master, then the master has the right to separate them or keep them together if he wishes, and if he wishes, he may take her away from him without divorce.

key_terms.بِغَيْرِ طَلَاقٍ: without divorce; without a formal pronouncement of divorce
key_terms.حُرَّةً: a free woman; a woman who is not enslaved
key_terms.طَلَاقُ: divorce; the legal dissolution of marriage
key_terms.مَوْلَاهُ: his master; the owner who holds authority in one of the described cases
key_terms.يَجْمَعَ: to keep together; to allow the marital union to remain
key_terms.يُفَرِّقَ: to separate; to cause the spouses to part
key_terms.ٱلْعَبْدِ: the slave; the male bondsman whose marital authority is being discussed

ai.seo_question: Who has the authority over divorce when a slave marries a free woman or a bondwoman?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning the authority over divorce in marriages involving a slave. It distinguishes between cases where the slave marries a free woman or another person's bondwoman, and cases where he marries his own master's bondwoman, in which the master's authority affects the continuation of the marriage.
